topic: 8 vision models benchmarked on one RTX 3090 (24 GB)
title: RTX 3090 still runs 8 vision models
description: One tester loaded 8 video vision models on a single RTX 3090 with 24 GB. The receipt says the oldest card is not the blocker for vision work. You'll learn what actually fits, what the wait costs, and when to keep the card. (Narration is AI-generated.)
hook_candidates: The oldest card in the tower beat the receipt
Eight vision models. One thirty ninety.
Your thirty ninety isn't obsolete. Its job changed.
One tester, one old card, eight models
The card upgrade videos buried just ran eight models
Keep the thirty ninety. The receipt says so.
Five years old and still the fastest decoder here
Obsolete for gaming was never obsolete for vision
narration_full: Your old RTX thirty ninety has receipts. The one upgrade videos call obsolete. One tester loaded eight video vision models, language models with eyes, onto one card. All eight ran. The biggest held thirty point eight billion parameters and wrote fastest: one hundred thirty-nine point three tokens per second. A mixture of experts: specialists behind a receptionist who wakes only the few each word needs. Memory from all of them, speed from the few. She re-picks every word. His own hedge: not a benchmark, an anecdotal reference. Worst wait: five point seven three seconds. Giant models don't fit. Long videos eat the KV cache, the running notes. So keep the card for vision work. A used one still costs nine hundred dollars, and it is not the blocker.
